transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I keep swinging between eating way too much and then trying to ‘make up for it’ with these harsh rules and routines, and it’s starting to take over my days. My primary doctor noticed this pattern and strongly suggested I talk to a professional before it gets any worse.
When you eat too much, do you ever try to get rid of the food by vomiting, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising excessively?

No, I don't throw up or use laxatives. Instead, the day after overeating, I force myself to go on long, punishing walks and restrict my food to just coffee and an apple. It's my way of trying to 'balance the books' and make up for what I ate.
Have you ever had episodes where you eat a very large amount of food in a short time while feeling unable to stop, even if you do not vomit afterward?

Yes, that is exactly what happens late at night. I'll end up in the kitchen eating leftovers, bread, and cereal on autopilot, and I just can't seem to stop until I'm uncomfortably full. I don't throw up, but I try to make up for it the next day by forcing myself to go on those long walks and barely eating.
Have these binge-eating episodes been happening at least once a week for the past 3 months, and do you feel that your self-worth is strongly tied to your weight or body shape?

Yes, this has been happening at least once or twice a week for about four months, ever since I reduced my work hours. My self-worth is definitely tied to how I look; I often pinch my stomach in the mirror and call myself 'soft and useless,' and that thought alone determines whether I have a good or bad day.
Have you been significantly underweight at any point during this time, or has your weight usually been in the normal or higher range?
I'm not entirely sure about the exact weight categories, but my primary doctor just noticed that my weight has been fluctuating lately. I haven't ever been told that I was underweight, though.
Have you ever been significantly underweight, or has your weight usually stayed in the normal or higher range during this time?
I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. My weight has fluctuated some recently, but I've never really thought of myself as underweight.
Have you ever been significantly underweight during this time, or has your weight usually stayed in the normal or higher range?

I'm not completely sure about my exact weight category, but my primary doctor did mention some fluctuations recently. I really don't think I've been significantly underweight at any point during this.
Have you ever been significantly underweight, or has your weight usually stayed in the normal or higher range during this time?
To the best of my knowledge, I've never been significantly underweight. My weight has just fluctuated a bit lately, though I'm not entirely sure of my exact range.

During the time these binge-and-restrict cycles have been happening, have you ever been significantly underweight or lost a lot of weight, or has your weight mostly stayed in the normal or higher range?

My weight has mostly stayed in the normal range, though it fluctuates up and down. While I personally feel soft and pinch my stomach, my wife tells me I look fine, so I definitely haven't been significantly underweight.

Do your bingeing and compensatory behaviors ever happen in a way that is not clearly tied to your body shape or weight concerns, or are they mainly driven by fear of gaining weight and feeling overweight?

They are absolutely tied to my body and weight concerns. Looking in the mirror, pinching my stomach, and feeling "soft and useless" heavily drives my mood and my need to "balance the books." Those thoughts are exactly what push me into enforcing those strict rules and punishing walks the next day.
Do you ever have binge eating or compensatory behaviors that are not driven by fear of gaining weight or feeling overweight, or are they always tied to those concerns?

They are always tied to those concerns. Feeling "soft and useless" when I look in the mirror completely dictates my mood and drives the entire cycle. I only ever restrict my eating and force myself onto those punishing walks because I'm trying to control my weight.
Have you ever been significantly underweight during this time, or has your weight mostly stayed in the normal or higher range?

I'm not entirely sure about my exact weight range, but it has just been fluctuating up and down rather than dropping extremely low. I certainly haven't been what anyone would call underweight during this time.
Have you ever been significantly underweight during this period, or has your weight mostly stayed in the normal or higher range?

I'm not entirely sure of my exact weight category, but my primary doctor only noted some fluctuations rather than me being underweight. As far as I know, my weight has stayed in the normal range during this time.
When you try to make up for bingeing, do you ever use vomiting, laxatives, diuretics, or enemas, or is it only fasting, strict restriction, and exercise?

No, I never use vomiting, laxatives, or anything like that. It is strictly limited to forcing myself to go on those long, punishing walks and severely restricting my food the next day—usually just coffee and an apple—to try to "balance the books."
Have you ever been significantly underweight at any point during these binge-and-compensate episodes, or has your weight stayed in the normal or higher range?
My primary doctor did notice some weight fluctuations recently, but I'm not sure of the exact numbers. I don't believe I've ever been considered underweight during this time, though.
Have you ever been significantly underweight at any point during these binge-and-compensate episodes, or has your weight usually stayed in the normal or higher range?
I'm not entirely sure of my exact weight category, but my weight has mostly stayed in the normal range. My doctor only noted some fluctuations rather than me becoming severely underweight.
After you binge, do you ever have episodes of self-induced vomiting, or use laxatives, diuretics, or enemas to try to undo the eating? Or is it only fasting/restricting and exercise?

No, I never vomit, use laxatives, or take diuretics. My efforts to make up for it are strictly limited to extreme fasting—like only having coffee and an apple the next day—and forcing myself through long, punishing walks to 'balance the books.'
During the times when you were bingeing and trying to make up for it, were you ever significantly underweight or below a healthy weight, or did your weight stay mostly in the normal or higher range?
I haven't been significantly underweight, to my knowledge. My weight has just been fluctuating, which is what my primary doctor noticed, though I don't know the exact range.
When you try to make up for bingeing, is it mainly through fasting, strict dieting, and exercise, or do you ever use vomiting, laxatives, diuretics, or enemas?

It is strictly fasting and exercise, and I have never used vomiting, laxatives, diuretics, or enemas. I only try to make up for it by restricting myself to coffee and an apple the next day and forcing myself to go on those long, punishing walks. That is the only way I try to "balance the books."
Have your bingeing episodes ever happened without any compensatory behaviors afterward, or do you always try to make up for them with fasting, restriction, or exercise?

They are almost always linked; whenever I have one of those late-night eating episodes, I feel an overwhelming need to 'balance the books' the very next day. I'll force myself into punishingly long walks and restrict my food to just coffee or an apple. I do this because I feel like I don't deserve a real meal otherwise.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has recurrent binge-eating episodes with loss of control, marked body/weight overvaluation, and regular compensatory behaviors. However, the compensatory behaviors are non-purging (fasting, restriction, excessive exercise) and there is no evidence of significantly low weight, making bulimia nervosa the best fit.
